linear.skipped: Skipped. Tasks start from prompts until you connect it.
linear.pending: Started: paste the app's values and authorize to finish.
linear.failed: Linear refused the token. Authorize the app again.

models.title: Models
models.lede: Any provider with an API base URL and a token. Names, logos, limits and prices come from the models.dev catalog. Agents reach a provider through ostra's key proxy, so its token never reaches the agent.
models.addLede: Test the connection first: ostra detects the API format and lists the models.
models.noProviders: No provider yet. Add one in the panel on the right.
models.name: Name
models.tokenHelp: Stored in the secret store, and never shown again.
models.formatHelp: Detected by the test. Correct it if the endpoint speaks the other one.
models.sessionsCapHelp: The most sessions that use this provider at the same time. Empty: no cap.
models.allowPersonalHelp: Off by default. A personal runner is a member's own machine: a key the key proxy holds there can be read by that member.
models.selectHint: Select a provider or a model to see its properties.
models.isDefault: The built-in OpenCode profile uses this model.
models.customTitle: Custom model: not in the catalog

reasoning.unsetNote: doesn't reason until an admin says
reasoning.priceFootnote: Reasoning priced apart: the catalog lists a separate price for this model's reasoning tokens. In v1, ostra prices reasoning tokens as output.
reasoning.tickSome: Tick the levels the endpoint takes, or Only on or off.
reasoning.catalogSaysNone: The catalog says it doesn't reason.
reasoning.confirmCatalog: Use the catalog's levels for {model}? Profiles and tasks on it will offer {levels}.
reasoning.droppedOne: 1 profile is set to {level}. Its tasks will run at {runAt}.
reasoning.droppedMany: {n} profiles are set to {level}. Their tasks will run at {runAt}.
reasoning.priceNote: Its catalog prices reasoning at {price} per million, apart from output. ostra v1 prices it as output.
reasoning.empty: No model yet. Add a provider, and the models its key lists show here.

github.title: GitHub
github.lede: A GitHub App opens every pull request, as its own bot, with the member as co-author. ostra mints a token for one repo at a time and never hands it to an agent.
github.privateKeyHelp: The App's PEM file. Paste it or pick the file. It goes to the secret store.
github.ownerHelp: Empty: the App belongs to your own GitHub account.
github.createHelp: GitHub asks you to confirm, then sends you back here.
github.noInstallations: The App isn't installed anywhere yet. Install it on GitHub, on the org that holds your repos.
github.noPublicAddress: This server's address isn't public, so the App is created without a webhook and receives no events. Set {setting} to turn them on.
github.reposFailed: GitHub did not list the installation's repos
github.permissionsHelp: checks and actions are asked for from the start, so no install re-approves later.
github.workflowsHelp: A push that touches {path} fails, and the task says why.

projects.title: Project
projects.newLede: A project is one repo and its environment. Tasks run against it and open their pull requests there.
projects.needsGitHubBody: A project's repo comes from the GitHub App's installation.
projects.name: Name
projects.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens make its slug.
projects.noRepos: The App sees no repository in this installation. Add one on GitHub.
projects.createHelp: Nothing runs yet. You review the environment next.
projects.reposSeen: The GitHub App sees {n} repositories in {account}.
projects.reposSeenOne: The GitHub App sees 1 repository in {account}.
projects.trackerNoneHelp: Tasks start from prompts typed in ostra.
projects.trackerLinearHelp: Tickets on a team's board become tasks.
projects.draftEmpty: Pick a repository to see what ostra finds in it.
projects.draftNote: Read from the repo's files. No agent, no model.
projects.draftFailed: You can still create the project and fill in the environment by hand.

environment.title: Environment
environment.lede: What every task of this project gets: its setup, the services beside it, and the checks after each turn.
environment.createdLede: ostra drafted this from the repo's files. Check it, fill in the secrets, and save.
environment.name: Name
environment.duringSetupHelp: Also available while the setup script runs.
environment.baseImageHelp: Applies on the docker executor only. Tasks on a personal runner (host) use the machine as it is.
environment.nothingFound: Nothing to go on: the repo has no lockfile or setup file ostra knows.
environment.servicesHelp: A service needs a container runtime, so a personal runner (host) doesn't start it. Services come with milestone 3.
environment.setupScriptNote: runs with bash in the task's workspace, before the agent starts
environment.noEntries: No variables, secrets or files yet.
environment.footnote: For dev and test credentials, never production ones. A secret reaches only its own repo's checkout.
environment.servicesShort: A personal runner doesn't start services. They come with milestone 3.

svc.title: Services
svc.note: start beside each box on docker runners, before the setup script
svc.empty: No services. Add one when tasks need a database or a cache beside them.
svc.runnerNoteOne: Host runners start no services, so this project's tasks run only on docker runners. {pools} has {count} online.
svc.runnerNoteMany: Host runners start no services, so this project's tasks run only on docker runners. {pools} have {count} online.
svc.runnerNoteNoPools: Host runners start no services, so this project's tasks run only on docker runners.
svc.blockedTitle: Tasks of this project are waiting.
svc.blockedOffline: It has services, and no runner online can start them. Host runners start none; a docker runner of {pools} can.
svc.blockedNoDocker: It has services, and none of this project's runners can start them: they all use the host executor. Remove the services, or add a docker runner to {pools}.
svc.name: Name
svc.healthCheckHelp: Runs in the service's container. Healthy when it exits 0.
svc.rebuildNote: Saving rebuilds the snapshot. Running tasks keep theirs.
svc.removeBody: New boxes start without it, and the snapshot rebuilds. Running tasks keep theirs.

chk.title: Checks
chk.note: run in this order after every turn with changes, before the push
chk.name: Name
chk.empty: No checks. Pull requests open without them.
chk.help: A failing check doesn't stop the push: the pull request opens as a draft, and the task page offers Ask the agent to fix.
chk.removeBody: It stops running after the next turn. Pull requests already open keep their state.

environment.footnoteServices: Services and checks get the environment's variables, never a model key or a GitHub token.

snap.failSecret: A setup secret was found in the image, so it was deleted
snap.noneHelp: A docker runner builds one after the next change, or with Rebuild. Until then each box runs the full setup.
snap.waiting: Waiting for a docker runner of this project's pools to come online.

runners.title: Runners
runners.ledeAdmin: Where tasks run. {online} of {total} runners online, {busy} of {slots} boxes busy, across {across}.
runners.ledeMember: Where tasks run. Your machine runs the tasks you send to it.
runners.noPools: No pools yet. A pool runs tasks on your servers; add one with New pool.
runners.noRunners: No runner has joined yet. Start one with a join token from a pool.
runners.connectAnother: Connect another machine: run this in a clone of ostra, then approve the code it prints.
runners.connectFirst: Connect your machine: run this in a clone of ostra, then approve the code it prints.
runners.hostNote: Personal runners use the host executor: the agent runs as a process on your machine, not isolated.
runners.hostNoteTreeOnly: A process the agent detaches isn't contained.
runners.shownOnce: Shown once. Stored only as a hash.
runners.revokeBody: Runners that already joined stay connected. No new runner can join with it.
runners.noPoolSelected: Select a pool to see its join tokens.
runners.poolRequiresApproval: Require approval for each new runner
runners.poolNameTaken: A pool with that name exists.

device.title: Approve a runner
device.lede: Enter the code ostra runner printed on your machine.
device.ledeConfirm: Check that this code matches the one in your terminal.
device.codeHelp: Letters and digits. The dash doesn't matter.
device.unknownCode: That code isn't known, or it expired. Run ostra runner again for a new one.
device.doesPersonal: It becomes your personal runner in {organization}.
device.doesOwnTasks: It runs only the tasks you send to it.
device.notIsolated: Personal, not isolated: the agent runs as a process on that machine, as you.
device.approveOnly: Approve only if you ran {command} yourself, just now. If you didn't, deny it.
device.failed: That didn't work. The code may have expired.
device.approved: Approved. The runner finishes signing in on its own, then shows on the Runners page.
device.denied: Denied. The runner can't sign in with that code.

task.imageRemote: Image not shown: it's on another server.
task.endedWithoutChanges: The session ended without changes: no pull request.
task.filesOutside: The agent left {count} outside the repositories: {names}. Reply to have them moved into a repository, or dismiss.
task.filesOutsideGone: No files are left outside the repositories now.
task.driverChanged: {name} is driving now ({by} handed it over)
task.unsupported: An event this panel doesn't know:

approval.title: Needs you · approval
approval.readOnly: The agent asked to run this. Answering comes in milestone 3.

system.workConflict: the unfinished work conflicts with the branch
system.previousLost: the box before it was lost
system.boxLost: The box was lost before the agent answered.

composer.label: Message the agent
composer.hint: Send queues. Interrupt and send stops the current turn.
composer.notDriver: {name} is driving. Take over to send messages.
composer.noDriver: Nobody is driving. Take over to send messages.

limit.stall: The agent stalled: nothing new for {n} minutes. The session stopped.
limit.max-duration: The session reached its maximum time of {n} minutes and stopped.
limit.spend-cap: The task reached its spend cap. The session stopped.

tasks.none: No tasks yet. Type a prompt above.

needsYouReason.question: Waiting for an answer
needsYouReason.environmentProposal: A change to the environment to review
needsYouReason.restoreConflict: Its saved work conflicts with the branch
needsYouReason.noProviderForModel: No provider serves its model in this project

effort.label: Effort
effort.reasoningTip: Counted inside out. Priced as output.
effort.markerDuringTurn: {name} set effort to {level}, from the next turn
effort.ranAt: Ran at {level}: this model has no {asked}.
effort.ranAtDefault: Ran at the default: this model takes no effort level.

newTask.title: New task
newTask.lede: Type what the agent should do. It works on its own branch and opens a pull request.
newTask.placeholder: Add a short CONTRIBUTING.md that explains how to run the tests
newTask.hostHelp: {runner} is your own machine. The agent runs in a worktree there, not isolated.
newTask.nextBox: A box of {repo} from {base}, on one of the project's pools
newTask.nextPr: It opens a pull request. Steer it while it runs, and reopen it any time.

taskPage.estimatedHelp: An endpoint reported no usage for a call, so the key proxy estimated its tokens.
taskPage.needsYouDefault: The agent stopped and waits on a person.

limit.title: Needs you · {what}
limit.stallBody: The agent produced nothing for a while, so ostra stopped the session. Its work is saved.
limit.max-durationBody: The session ran for its maximum time, so ostra stopped it. Its work is saved.
limit.spend-capBody: The task spent {spent} of its {cap} cap, so ostra stopped the session. Raise the cap to reopen it.
limit.spend-capTokens: The task used {spent} tokens of its {cap} cap, so ostra stopped the session. Raise the cap to reopen it.
limit.crashedBody: The session ended without finishing. Its work up to the last turn is saved.
limit.boxLostBody: The box was lost before the agent answered. Reopen to carry on in a fresh box.

restoreConflict.title: Needs you · restore conflict
restoreConflict.body: The unfinished work saved after the last turn conflicts with commits pushed to the branch since. Nothing was restored from it; the agent carries on from the branch's head.
restoreConflict.footnote: The saved work stays until the box is released at the end of the task.

composer.idleHint: The session is idle in the same box. Send starts the next turn.
composer.reopenHint: Reopening picks a runner, restores the session and keeps the same branches and PRs.
composer.startingHint: The task is starting. You can send once the agent is ready.
composer.mergedHint: Its pull requests are merged. Start a new task from the ticket to change it again.
composer.openInInbox: Open the ticket in the Inbox
composer.spendCap: This task reached its spend cap. It can't be reopened until the cap is raised.
composer.ticketHasTask: The ticket already has an active task.

taskPage.servicesWait: Waiting for a runner that can start services. Online now: {runners}.
taskPage.servicesWaitNone: Waiting for a runner that can start services. None is online.

linear.title: Linear
linear.lede: The organization's own Linear app reads tickets and writes back status, one comment and links. Its tokens stay on this server, in the secret store, and never reach an agent.

connect.title: Connect your Linear app
connect.disconnectedFrom: Disconnected from {workspace} on {date}. Its boards and tickets stay, read-only.

step1.title: Create the app in Linear
step1.body: ostra fills in the app's name, its callback and its webhook. You press Create in Linear, as a workspace admin.

step2.title: Paste the app's values
step2.body: From the app's page in Linear. They go to the secret store and are never shown again.

step3.title: Authorize
step3.body: Linear asks you to install the app on the workspace, then sends you back here.

mode.label: Mode
mode.sendsToServer: Linear will send events to this server, at
mode.pollingLine: This server's address isn't public ({reason}), so the app gets no webhook and ostra asks Linear for changes every {seconds} s. Set {setting} to a public https address to receive events.
mode.pollingLineNoReason: This server's address isn't public, so the app gets no webhook and ostra asks Linear for changes every {seconds} s. Set {setting} to a public https address to receive events.
mode.webhooksHelp: Linear sends each change to this server as it happens.

events.title: Events
events.silentHelp: Check the app's webhook in Linear: it may be disabled, or its URL may have changed. Tickets still arrive every {minutes} min.
events.webhookNone: None: this server's address isn't public ({reason}).
events.webhookNoneNoReason: None: this server's address isn't public.
events.backstopBody: Every board is also polled every {minutes} min, so a missed delivery is found.

token.title: Token
token.expiresIn: · expires in {left}, refreshed an hour before
token.failed: Linear refused the refresh. Polling and writes have stopped.
token.memberAuthorize: An admin authorizes the app again.
token.apiKeyBody: A personal API key from the server's settings. It never refreshes.

disconnect.title: Disconnect
disconnect.body: Revokes the token at Linear and stops every board. Boards and their tickets stay, read-only.
disconnect.confirmBody: ostra revokes its token at Linear and stops polling and webhooks for every board. Boards, tickets and tasks stay, read-only. To connect again, you authorize the app again.

panel.eventsHelp: AgentSessionEvent is asked for now, so agent mode later needs no new app.

storage.title: Storage
storage.lede: Where ostra keeps files, and how long it keeps a finished task's history.

store.title: Blob store
store.note: session archives, ticket images and attachments
store.help: To move new blobs to an S3-compatible store, set {store} and its five {s3} settings, then restart. Blobs already stored stay readable where they are.
store.helpS3: Blobs stored in Postgres before the switch stay readable from there.

retention.title: Retention
retention.lede: How long a finished task keeps its history, archives and blobs.
retention.keep: As long as the task exists
retention.invalid: A whole number of days, from 1 to 3650.
retention.willDelete1: On save, every night ostra deletes these for tasks finished more than {days} days ago:
retention.willDelete2: events and messages, live text, session archives, ticket images and attachments.
retention.willDelete3: The task, its repos and its pull request links stay. A reopened task says its history was removed.
retention.audit: Changes are recorded in the audit log.
retention.fromEnv: From OSTRA_RETENTION_DAYS. Saving here overrides it.
retention.confirmOffBody: Nothing more is deleted. What earlier sweeps deleted stays deleted.

panel.neverChanged: Never changed. Retention is off by default.

repos.title: Repos

blocked.title: Tasks can't start in this project.
blocked.one: {repo} requires signed commits, which ostra doesn't support yet.
blocked.many: {n} repos require signed commits, which ostra doesn't support yet.

check.notProtectedWhy: Allowed: the agent holds no token, and ostra pushes only the task's own branch.
check.signedRequiredWhy: ostra's pushes aren't signed, so GitHub would refuse them.
check.noReason: The code host didn't say why.

repos.footnote: ostra reads each default branch's rules when you open this page, at most every 10 minutes, and again when a task starts.

panel.whyAllowedBody: The agent never holds a GitHub token. ostra's git proxy accepts pushes only to the task's branch and its hidden ref, so {branch} stays out of the agent's reach. Protecting {branch} still guards it from everyone else.
panel.whyBlockedBody: GitHub refuses commits that aren't signed on this branch, and ostra can't sign the agent's commits yet. Until it can, no task starts in this project.
panel.whyUnknownAfter: ostra checks again when a task starts. A task isn't refused because of a check it couldn't make.
panel.protectStep1: On GitHub, open the repo's Settings › Rules.
panel.protectStep2: Add a ruleset for {branch} that requires a pull request.
panel.toStartBody: Turn off "Require signed commits" for {branch} on GitHub, or remove this repo from the project.
panel.openRules: Open the repo's rules on GitHub

composer.unsupported: {repo} requires signed commits, which ostra doesn't support yet.
composer.unprotected: {repo}'s default branch isn't protected. Tasks still start: the agent can't push to it.

ticketTemplate.title: Ticket template
ticketTemplate.lede: The first prompt of a task started from a ticket. Ticket text always goes inside marked blocks, so the agent reads it as data, never as instructions.
ticketTemplate.readOnly: Only a project admin can change it.
ticketTemplate.resetTitle: Go back to the built-in template?
ticketTemplate.resetBody: Your custom template is replaced. Tasks already started keep the prompt they got.

describe.ticket_priority: Its priority, when it has one
describe.ticket_description: Its description, in a marked block
describe.images: Each image copied into the workspace

preview.title: Preview
preview.empty: The Inbox has no ticket to preview on. {link} to the project first.
preview.note: Rendered on the server for this page only. Never logged.

boards.title: Boards
boards.lede: Linear teams whose tickets reach this project's Inbox. Each board maps ostra's steps to the team's statuses.
boards.readOnly: Only the project's admins change boards.
boards.noConnection: This organization isn't connected to Linear yet.
boards.askAdmin: Ask an admin to connect Linear.

attached.title: Attached
attached.none: No boards yet. Attach a team, and its open tickets fill the Inbox.
attached.detachBody: ostra stops polling {key}. Its tickets stay in the Inbox's history and its tasks keep their links, but no new task starts from it.
attached.justAttached: Attached. The first poll is filling the Inbox.

mapping.title: Status mapping
mapping.note: Drafted from Linear's status types. Every status of the team is in each picker.
mapping.noMapping: This board has no mapping yet. Pick a status for each step.
mapping.openEmpty: Pick at least one status, or the Inbox stays empty.
mapping.gone: This status is gone from Linear. Pick another.

next.title: What the next task does on the ticket
next.started: When the task starts, ostra moves it to {status} and comments once with a link to the task.
next.inReview: At the first PR, ostra moves it to {status} and links the PR.
next.inReviewSame: At the first PR, the ticket stays in {status}, and ostra links the PR.
next.doneIntegration: When the last PR merges, Linear's GitHub integration moves it to {status}. ostra doesn't.
next.doneOstra: When the last PR merges, ostra moves it to {status}.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.ledeMany: Open tickets from {n} boards on Linear
inbox.ledeNoBoards: Open tickets from this project's boards, ready to become tasks.
inbox.stale: Linear isn't answering. These are the tickets as of {age}.

empty.noConnectionBody: An admin connects Linear once for the organization. Then a project attaches its teams as boards.
empty.noBoardsBody: Attach a Linear team to this project, and its open tickets show here.
empty.nothingOpenMany: Nothing open on this project's boards
empty.nothingOpenBody: New tickets show here as they arrive.

panel.context: The agent gets the title, the description and the labels{extra}.
panel.unsupported: {repo} requires signed commits, which ostra doesn't support yet.

approval.name: Approvals
approval.description: The agent wants to do something its rules hold back

question.name: Questions

plan.description: A plan is ready to approve

pr_ready.description: A draft pull request waits for review

crashed.description: The agent stopped with an error

spend_cap.description: The task used its whole spend cap

setup_failed.description: A setup command failed on the box

ticket_closed.name: Ticket closed
ticket_closed.description: The ticket closed while the task ran

notificationSettings.title: Notifications
notificationSettings.lede: When a task needs you, ostra tells you here, on the ticket and by mail. Choose which moments reach you where.
notificationSettings.mailOff: Mail is off on this install.
notificationSettings.mailOffBody: Your email choices are kept, and apply once an instance admin sets up mail.
notificationSettings.footnote: The panel always shows every moment. Ticket comments go only to tasks with a ticket.
notificationSettings.addressHintTracker: Your sign-in address. {tracker} mentions use it too.
notificationSettings.mailCarries: A mail carries the task's title and key, the moment, one line about it and a link. Never ticket text, agent output or code.
notificationSettings.neverChanged: Never changed. These are the defaults.

email.title: Email
email.lede: How ostra mails members when a task needs them. The panel and the ticket work without it.
email.offLine: Members see what needs them in the panel and on the ticket. Their notification pages say mail is off.
email.smtpHelp: Port 587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with TLS, works with most providers.
email.resendHelp: A key with sending access, from your Resend account. The from address's domain must be verified there.
email.senderHelp: Use an address on a domain your mail provider has verified, or mail may be refused.
email.saveToTest: Save your changes to test them.
email.noAddress: Your account has no email address.
email.accepted: Accepted by {provider} at {time}. Check {address} for it.
email.footnote: Secrets go to the secret store and are never shown again. Changes are recorded in the audit log.
email.locked: Set by {settings} on this install. Change them there and restart ostra.
email.readOnly: Only the instance admin can change email.

invalid.security: Without TLS, only a mail server on this machine is allowed.
invalid.apiKey: A Resend API key starts with re_.

email.neverChanged: Never changed. Mail is off by default.

fix.one: Sends this check's output to {agent} as the next turn.
fix.several: Sends the {n} failing checks' output to {agent} as the next turn.
fix.afterTurn: Sends it to {agent} after the current turn.
fix.reopen: Sending reopens the task with the output.

pr.name: PR #{n}
pr.draftByOstra: because a check failed after turn {n}. ostra marks it ready when every check passes.
pr.draftByPerson: on GitHub, so it stays one when the checks pass.

checks.footnote: Checks run after every turn that changes the code, before the push. They come from the project's environment.
checks.noneBody: Checks are commands from the project's environment that run after every turn that changes the code.
checks.notYet: Checks run after the first turn that changes the code.
checks.oldRunner: This task's runner doesn't run checks. Update the runner to get them.

takeLocal.title: Take it local
takeLocal.lede: Check out this task's branches on your machine. Git fetches them with your own access; ostra hands out no token.
takeLocal.firstTime: First time on this machine? Run {command}, then approve its code in the browser.
takeLocal.merged: PR #{n} is merged. GitHub may have deleted its branch.
takeLocal.reopen: Reopening the task starts from the branches as they are, your commits included.
takeLocal.nothingPushed: Nothing to check out yet. A branch appears after the first turn with changes.
takeLocal.copyRefused: Select the text and copy it

account.title: Account
account.lede: Your GitHub account, and the machines where you ran ostra login. Only you see this page.

github.title: GitHub
github.note: for co-author credit, and for @ostra on a pull request
github.helpLinked: ostra kept your GitHub login and ID, and revoked the sign-in token at once.
github.helpNotLinked: Link the GitHub account you work with. ostra keeps only your login and ID, and revokes the sign-in token at once. Until then, commits from your tasks credit your ostra name and email, and @ostra from your GitHub account isn't answered.
github.notConnected: GitHub isn't connected to this install yet.
github.askAdmin: Ask an admin to connect GitHub.

back.taken: That GitHub account is linked to another ostra account. Unlink it there first.
back.revokeFailed: GitHub didn't confirm the token was revoked, so ostra stored nothing. Try again.
back.failed: The link didn't finish. Nothing was stored.

github.unlinkBody: @ostra from this GitHub account stops reaching the agent, and new commits credit your ostra name and email. You can link again at any time.

cli.title: CLI sessions

note.one: made by ostra login, valid for {n} day
note.other: made by ostra login, valid for {n} days

cli.none: No CLI sessions. Run the line below on a machine to start one.
cli.another: Sign in another machine: run this in a clone of ostra, then approve the code it prints.
cli.first: Sign in a machine: run this in a clone of ostra, then approve the code it prints.
cli.footnote: A CLI session reads only a task's branches and clone URLs. Git uses your own access: ostra hands out no token.
cli.revokeBody: ostra checkout on that machine stops working until it runs ostra login again.

changes.updateTitle: Ask the agent to merge {base} into the task's branch and fix any conflicts.
changes.nothingPushed: Nothing pushed yet. The diff shows here after the agent's first turn that changes code.
changes.noNewline: No newline at end of file
changes.onlyYou: Only you see a draft until you send it.
changes.lineGone: This line changed since you opened it. Copy your comment and reload the diff.

review.idle: Sent together as one message. The session is idle, so they start the next turn.
review.steer: Sent together as one message. {agent} reads them at its next step.
review.afterTurn: Sent together as one message, after the current turn.
review.reopen: Sent together as one message. Sending reopens the task.
review.notDriver: {name} is driving. Take over to send your comments.
review.tooMany: At most 50 comments go in one message. Delete some to send the rest.

afterMerge.freshBranch: Reopened after the merge on a fresh branch, {branch}, from {base}.

needsYouPage.heading: Needs you
needsYouPage.lede: What waits on you across your projects. {n} unread.
needsYouPage.ledeNone: What waits on you across your projects.
needsYouPage.emptyBody: Approvals, questions and plans show here first, and on Home.
needsYouPage.mailOff: Mail is off on this install
needsYouPage.mailNote: A mail waits {n} minutes and isn't sent once you've read it here.
needsYouPage.deliveryFailedMail: The mail didn't send: {error}. ostra retries.
needsYouPage.deliveryFailedTicket: The ticket comment didn't post: {error}. ostra retries.
needsYouPage.driving: {name} is driving. Open the task to take over.
needsYouPage.forThisTaskAdds: For this task adds {pattern} to the task's rules. Any member of {project} can answer.

agentProfiles.title: Agent profiles
agentProfiles.lede: An agent, its model, and what it works with: instructions, skills, MCP servers and the rules that ask a person first. A project picks one per kind of task, and members pick from the ones they may use.
agentProfiles.onlyBuiltIn: Only the built-in profile so far. A profile of your own sets the model, instructions, skills and rules a task starts with.
agentProfiles.pickHint: Pick a profile to see its setup.

panel.noRules: No rules: the agent asks nobody.
panel.noModelLine: A task can't start with it until it has a model.

editor.lede: Its permissions and MCP servers win over a repo's own agent config. Its instructions and skills sit beside the repo's.
editor.name: Name
editor.instructionsNote: added beside the repo's AGENTS.md, never replacing it
editor.instructionsPlaceholder: What every task with this profile should know, on top of the repo's own instructions.
editor.skillsNote: written to the task's own config folder, never to the repo
editor.noSkills: No skills. A skill is a SKILL.md and up to 20 files the agent reads when it needs them.
editor.mcpNote: reached through the runner's MCP proxy, so no secret enters the box
editor.rulesNote: the agent waits until a member approves
editor.noRules: No rules: the agent asks nobody. Add a preset or a rule of your own.
editor.footnote: A rule keeps a person in the loop. It doesn't contain the agent: a command can still write a file an edit rule watches. The box contains it.

effort.label: Effort
effort.help: How long {model} thinks before it acts. Its own levels.
effort.note: A running task keeps its own level. A change here applies to new tasks.
effort.noReasoning: {model} doesn't take an effort level. Tasks run at the endpoint's default.
effort.stored: Saved as {saved}. {model} has no {saved}, so new tasks run at {runAt}.
effort.unsetCustom: Nobody has said whether {model} reasons, so tasks run without an effort level.
effort.agentNone: {agent} doesn't take an effort level. Tasks run at the model's default.

rules.name: Name
rules.matchesNone: Matches none of the sample paths.
rules.matchesNoneCommands: Matches none of the sample commands.
rules.matchesAll: Asks for every request of this tool.
rules.errorGlobs: Give the rule at least one glob.
rules.errorCommands: Give the rule at least one command.

skill.name: Name
skill.nameHelp: The folder name the agent sees.
skill.filesHelp: Up to 20 files, at most 1 MiB each.
skill.errorName: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes only.
skill.errorTaken: Another skill already has that name.
skill.errorCount: A skill holds at most 20 files.

server.name: Name
server.headersHelp: Values go to the secret store and are never shown again. The runner's MCP proxy adds them; the agent sees only the proxy's address.
server.commandHelp: A command already in the box's image.
server.envHelp: No secrets here: a server that needs one runs as an HTTP server behind the proxy.
server.readOnlyHelp: Its tools only read. Plan mode may call them, and "Reaching the network" doesn't ask for them.
server.errorName: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes only.
server.errorTaken: Another server already has that name.

props.planFirstHelp: The first turn only reads and proposes a plan. The driver approves it before anything changes.
props.whoHelp: Organization admins can use every profile.
props.builtInHelp: The built-in profile is open to everyone, so every project has a default to fall back on.
props.nobodyListed: Add at least one member, or choose Everyone.
props.archiveHelpNone: No project defaults to it. Archived, it leaves every picker.
props.archiveHelpOne: 1 project defaults to it. Archived, it leaves every picker.
props.archiveHelpMany: {n} projects default to it. Archived, it leaves every picker.
props.archiveBody: It leaves every picker, and nobody can start a task with it. Tasks that used it keep their record.
props.archiveMoves: {project} defaults to it for {kind}: those start with {builtIn} until an admin picks another.

projectDefaults.title: Agent profiles
projectDefaults.help: The profile a task of each kind starts with. Only profiles open to every member of the project are offered.

taskAnswers.forTaskAdds: Approve for this task also approves later requests that match: {rule}.
taskAnswers.anyMember: Any member of {project} can answer. The first answer wins.

deny.label: Reason for {agent} (optional)
deny.otherOne: The other open approval closes as cancelled.
deny.otherMany: The {n} other open approvals close as cancelled.

question.driverFoot: {agent} waits for your answer. Only the driver answers questions.
question.nobody: Nobody is driving. Take over to answer.

plan.title: Needs you · plan
plan.whatChange: What should change in the plan?
plan.driverFoot: {agent} works from the plan once it's approved, and changes nothing before.
plan.revisionAsked: {name} asked for changes; the agent is revising the plan.

watcher.hint: Any member can answer approvals. Take over to send messages.

ticketClosed.title: Needs you · ticket closed
ticketClosed.body: The ticket was closed while the task ran, so its turn was interrupted.

hints.default: The endpoint's own default. ostra sends nothing.
hints.minimal: Barely any thinking. Nearly as fast as off.
hints.low: A little thinking. Quick and cheap.
hints.high: Thinks longer on hard steps. Slower, costs more.
hints.xhigh: The deepest thinking. Slowest and costliest.
hints.max: As much thinking as the model allows. Slowest and costliest.
hints.on: Thinks before it acts. The model has no levels, only on or off.
hints.xhighBesideMax: Very deep thinking. Slow and costly.
